attribution: Halborn Security (report author); extracted by the VLUN pipeline; this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: The Halborn Security Public Reports collection is a GitHub repository of customer engagement write-ups, mostly PDFs, each carrying a scope table, a findings section with a reported severity, and a contacts page naming the Halborn staff who worked the engagement. From the pinned commit recorded for this source, the VLUN pipeline registered 1,785 finding-level rows. No LICENSE file was found in that repository, so the terms of the write-ups themselves are unstated rather than permissive, and the contacts pages put named individuals' work addresses into every PDF that was text-mined. The distribution view keeps the pointers, the reported severity, the language and the report hash, and drops the mined passages and the mailboxes.

attribution: Oak Security (report author); licence term as recorded in V4/manifest.json; this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: Oak Security publishes completed audit reports per project in a public GitHub repository. The VLUN manifest records the repository's own notice as CC BY-ND 4.0, which permits sharing with attribution but forbids distributing derivative works. Text-mining a report into shorter fields and re-laying it beside other sources is a derivative of it, so the copied passages cannot be redistributed on that term even though attribution is present. 3,257 finding-level rows were registered from the pinned commit; the distribution view keeps their pointers, page locators and report hashes and withholds the passages.

attribution: CoinFabrik (report author); this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: CoinFabrik publishes a smaller set of wallet, protocol and tooling assessments. The VLUN manifest records that no LICENSE file was found for that collection, and 226 finding-level rows were registered from the pinned commit. Because nothing states the terms, the conservative reading is all-rights-reserved: metadata and links are safe to carry, passages are not.

attribution: protocol authors (code); Code4rena (contest); this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: Five of the eight Code4rena protocol repositories cited by the v1 derived layer ship no LICENSE file at the commit the dataset pins (NOYA, Decent, Alchemix, Panoptic and GTE Perps). 424 of the 722 derived records quote Solidity taken from those repositories, which is 895 quotation entries in total. Quoting a short excerpt for commentary and offering the same text for onward redistribution are different acts, and no permission from those protocol authors is on file, so the quoted text is dropped from the distribution view and replaced by the file, commit, line range, permalink and the hash of the bytes that were removed. The remaining three repositories (reNFT, BakerFi, Wildcat) are source-available under terms that permit use but not redistribution; their citations were already reference-only.

attribution: Code4rena submission authors (PoC code); this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: The proof-of-concept tests in the v1 layers were written by contest participants, not by this project; 346 derived records carry such source. A few carry the author's own SPDX line, most carry none. This project neither owns that code nor received permission to sublicense it, so the distribution view carries the test name, framework, file, recorded impact and the hash of the removed text instead of the text.

attribution: reNFT (repository author); this summary is the VLUN authors' own wording
text: Running the reNFT proofs required test-tree files that only exist in the audited repository. Those files were compiled locally and are not published; each experiment directory carries a WITHHELD.json naming the file, its byte count, the sha256 of the exact bytes that were compiled and the commit to read them from, which keeps a replay byte-verifiable without redistributing source-available code.
